name: Amram
overview: Amram is a male member of the tribe of Levi, uniquely identified as the son of Kohath. His lineage situates him within the Levitical family, which held significant roles in Israel's religious history. There are no additional notes recorded about him beyond his genealogical position.
namesAndTitles: The name Amram means 'exalted people,' reflecting a noble or elevated status among his descendants. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a meaningful Hebrew significance.
familyAndRelationships: Amram is explicitly recorded as the son of Kohath. He is also the husband of Jochebed, and the father of Aaron, Moses, and Miriam. These relationships are either explicitly stated or reasonably inferred from the scriptural references provided.
scriptureSignificance: Amram's importance in the biblical narrative lies chiefly in his role as the patriarch of key figures in Israel's history—Aaron, Moses, and Miriam—who were instrumental in God’s deliverance of Israel from Egypt and the establishment of the covenant community. His Levitical heritage through Kohath connects him to the priestly tribe, underscoring the spiritual legacy passed to his children. Thus, Amram serves as a foundational link in the lineage through which God's redemptive plan unfolds.
